scope: 6ixSummit Labs marketing homepage and search/social metadata
diagnosis: Substantive rewrite: founder jargon, repeated slogans and unsupported speed or availability claims obscured the service offer. Keep the portfolio, brand identity and broader software services; make the current small-business audience easier to recognise.

skills.installation: Install the two paths at the pinned revision with Codex's skill-installer. The installed copies include their references, LICENSE and UPSTREAM.json.

context.business: 6ixSummit Labs is an early-stage design and software studio.
context.primaryAudience: Small-business owners who need a first website or a better one. Current outreach targets Regina, Edmonton and Calgary; that pilot does not establish a geographic service restriction.
secondaryAudiences: Teams that need custom tools or automation
context.primaryAction: Email the team about a project. Header, hero and services links lead to the contact section; the contact action opens an email.
proof: The user supplied Ayoé Event House and AKILI Development Group as portfolio projects.
Existing approved site content describes LuxeStyleBraids booking, deposit and owner-dashboard features.
AKILI's public website presents English/French content and project and construction management services.
The project contains custom CRM and automation work, ASA homepage authoring and VectorCraft logo workflows.
limits: Portfolio descriptions explain features; they do not establish customer revenue, conversion lift or time saved.
No verified customer interviews or testimonial quotes are available for this rewrite.
No exclusive advantage over named competing studios has been established. Avoid best, fastest or unique claims.
Working practices describe the proposed service process. Delivery dates, price, ownership terms and support scope belong in the agreed project terms.

sectionAnnotations.reason: Name websites immediately, then explain booking tools, apps and automation through recognisable uses. The service strip replaces unverified numerical promises.
Lead with business websites, retain design, AI, web apps and mobile services, and describe what a customer or team can do with each.
Keep all three named projects and describe the work. Remove developer-stack jargon and current booking-activity claims.
Explain scope, design review, development and handover without committing every project to one timetable. Preserve existing brands and make review points clear.
Give small-business owners a clear entry point while keeping first-version product and internal-tool work visible.
Invite an email containing the business and project idea. Match the button to the actual email action and remove unverified availability pressure.

claimsRemoved.claim: Six-week first release and standard service delivery ranges
claimsRemoved.evidenceNeededToRestore: Agreed service packages, scope assumptions and delivery terms supported by the team's capacity.

claimsRemoved.claim: Two build slots open this quarter
claimsRemoved.evidenceNeededToRestore: A current capacity record and a date when the claim must be refreshed or removed.
Comparable completed-project records supporting the speed comparison.

claimsRemoved.claim: Every-Friday delivery and automatic fixed pricing
claimsRemoved.evidenceNeededToRestore: The actual delivery cadence and commercial policy agreed for the advertised offer.

claimsRemoved.claim: A scope, timeline and price after one thirty-minute call
claimsRemoved.evidenceNeededToRestore: A defined consultation offer that can reliably fulfil that promise.

headlines.text: A website that feels like your business.
headlines.rationale: A more personal direction if the visual identity offer becomes the main emphasis.

headlines.text: Help customers get to know your business.
headlines.rationale: Focuses on the visitor's task; the supporting line must still name website design and development.

callsToAction.rationale: An alternative for links to the contact section.
An explicit alternative for the email action.

editingSweeps.clarity: Replace MVP, evals and internal engineering language with website, app, booking and workflow examples.
editingSweeps.voice: Use plain, conversational language; remove repeated climbing metaphors and agency put-downs.
editingSweeps.customerBenefit: Connect the offer to showing services, receiving enquiries and managing work.
editingSweeps.proof: Use named portfolio work. Add no invented metrics, reviews, guarantees or scarcity.
editingSweeps.specificity: Describe features and review steps instead of adding unsupported numbers.
editingSweeps.emotion: Respect the owner's existing business and identity; invite a rough idea without implying they need technical expertise.
editingSweeps.nextStep: Say what to email and use an email-labelled button. Scope and ongoing support are discussed rather than assumed.

verification.type: Editorial and browser review, not a conversion experiment
verification.screenshots: Temporary review files stay outside the repository.
